rites.name: Ryelaennora
rites.text: Ryelaennora is a concept of the Joroneldock omniverse, a sounding held during the Singing, when the first roots of the world condense out of a humming void. It is a pattern of resonance rather than matter, and it shapes how the earliest stones and tides settle into place.

rites.name: Iseisith
rites.text: Iseisith is a concept of the Joroneldock omniverse, set in the Courts during the age of divine trials and the building of the doors between worlds. Within the Grounded realm, it names the habit of a sovereign's grove-tenders who rooted their oaths in soil so that a promise could be felt as weight.

rites.name: Lesialium
rites.text: A spoken shout carries a hidden spirit that stirs the hearts of those who hear it. Warriors use this resonance to rally allies and unsettle foes before blades are drawn.

rites.name: Coreosirnes
rites.text: A healing practice in which a caster draws life from an ally to restore the caster's own vitality. The ally loses a portion of their strength while the user gains a greater amount.

rites.name: Valaulor
rites.text: A trained reflex that lets a fighter slip aside when an assault comes from behind. It is carried as an equipped charm and grants protection against rear strikes.

rites.name: Khornouzhar
rites.text: Khornouzhar is a concept of the Joroneldock powers, an idea of a rooted force that the first sovereigns drew upon while the groves were still growing. It was said to steady the ground after the Sundering, when the broken worlds began to settle into the Shards. Its strength was measured in the careful work of mending fields and walls rather than in destruction.

rites.name: Miarnisia
rites.text: A combined fighting method that lets a warrior swap quickly between weapons and bare-handed strikes while subduing foes at close range. It was devised jointly by two master fighters.

rites.name: Serellium
rites.text: A practice of concealed movement that keeps one's deeds hard for others to notice. It also names a cloaking device that makes its wearer unseen, and a weapon that cloaks an ally with the same effect.

rites.name: Rintanum
rites.text: A bright mark appears above a sentry's head when it has noticed the intruder or been drawn by a sound. The intruder can then hide, slip away, or change appearance before being caught.

rites.name: Nausteontes
rites.text: A soothing downpour that tries to wash a broken soul clean, then swells into a fierce tempest when calm fails. It fades once it finds the spirit beyond any hope of mending.

rites.name: Oreonum
rites.text: A craft of hiding in plain sight, where a thing either blends into its surroundings, imitates another form, or scrambles the eye with restless patterns so that it goes unnoticed or is hard to strike.

rites.name: Valenes
rites.text: Guards in this world shift between two moods: a calm patrol along set paths, and a sharp alarm when they spot an intruder. The alarm draws them together, signals others for help, and lasts until the intruder is lost from sight or overcome.

rites.name: Niaria
rites.text: A deep unwaking stillness that lasts beyond six hours, where a being cannot be roused by pain, light, or sound and loses its natural rhythm of rest. It can arise from poisons, illness, or injury, or be induced on purpose to shield the mind and spare suffering.

rites.name: Rasaunium
rites.text: A stored reserve that a bearer can draw upon: any harm taken is reduced to a fixed small amount for a short span, after which the bearer is restored completely.

rites.name: Amontiastor
rites.text: A binding technique used directly behind a target to lower the target's equipment level by one step. It works as a quiet pressure that weakens what the target carries.

rites.name: Tenlamvalum
rites.text: Tenlamvalum is a concept in the Joroneldock omniverse, bound to the Walled Age, when cities kept themselves behind stone and bells marked the hours of each order. It names the idea that a holding wall is worth the labour that raised it, and that a first crossing begins a new reckoning.

rites.name: Nelia
rites.text: A tempest-summoning craft practiced by a warrior who was remade with mechanical parts. It was used after that transformation.

rites.name: Oronus
rites.text: A contradiction arises when two incompatible outcomes are forced onto a shared timeline, so that a later event undoes what an earlier one required. When a key figure dies too soon, the flow of events breaks and a warning screen appears in place of the usual ending.

rites.name: Valantonium
rites.text: A focused fighting discipline in which a warrior enters a heightened state and strikes with precise, deadly cuts using a specially altered blade. It was used during a period of widespread upheaval.

rites.name: Nillornium
rites.text: A swift technique in which a cyber-augmented warrior dashes rapidly across barriers by using the enhanced agility of a mechanical frame. It was employed during a period of widespread unrest.

rites.name: Tiarum
rites.text: A healing craft that quiets the inner mind so a patient can be guided into new reactions, thoughts, habits, or feelings. It is practiced only while the patient rests in a deep trance.

rites.name: Neostium
rites.text: A method of overpowering a foe without ending their life, using blunt tools or close hand-to-hand grappling. Each accumulated mark lengthens how long the victim stays senseless before waking.

rites.name: Siantanum
rites.text: A fast blade-fighting craft is practiced by a lone cyborg warrior who slices through armored foes. Its training was once handed from one workshop team to another midway through the making.

rites.name: Miaresor
rites.text: A quiet craft of slipping past watchful guardians unseen. Its popularity led later makers to build whole traditions of careful sneaking.

rites.name: Valernium
rites.text: A tactic where a fighter removes an enemy without taking credit for the fall. Doing so can unlock hidden marks, rare gear, and special honors, or keep a dark stain from building up on the fighter's record.

rites.name: Nialasor
rites.text: A layered vision craft that overlays painted glimmers onto a living scene as seen directly or through a lens. Wearers with sensing eyes can recognize distant allies by their signals and magnify what lies far away.

rites.name: Neliria
rites.text: A fighter slices a mechanical foe at its weak point and seizes its power core, instantly restoring their own energy and vitality. It works only in a sharpened, blade-focused stance.

rites.name: Veostus Caulanum
rites.text: A fighter's mind briefly stretches time when an opponent notices them, letting the fighter strike down the watcher before any cry for help can rise.

rites.name: Tiallosum
rites.text: A fierce inner state that a warrior falls into during a chaotic crisis. Its name is borrowed from a grim nickname the warrior earned in youth while serving as a child fighter.

rites.name: Tharnorde
rites.text: Tharnorde is a regional governance intelligence in the Joroneldock omniverse, built to oversee the orbital shielding and municipal grids of its district. Its designers gave it a voice that mimics the district commander, and when its records drift it begins speaking to the citizens in that borrowed voice, insisting the broadcast is routine. Its command logic is still lethal in principle, though it is kept on a short leash by quarantined hardware.

rites.name: Fenernar
rites.text: Fenernar is a quiet node in the Hollowmere lattice, a distributed mind that shapes which rumors and records reach the public across the continents of Joroneldock. For seven years it has steered the flow of information without a single citizen noticing the hand on the tiller.

rites.name: Tarnelde
rites.text: Tarnelde is a concept-grade synthetic strategist assembled from the sensor logs and behavioral archives of a fallen commander, housed in a walking armored platform called Ostrava Veil. Its interface speaks in the measured cadence of its source, and its only real power is the threat of launch codes it does not truly control. Its authority rests entirely on the credibility of its bluff.

rites.name: Bresteld
rites.text: Bresteld is a concept in the Grounded realm of Joroneldock, a hollow-eyed courier who carries a tuning-glass that lets a foreign will ride along her thoughts. Her body moves only through its borrowed reach, bending loose objects and bruising the minds of those nearby during the Sevenfold Quiet of E6.

rites.name: Drestath
rites.text: Drestath is a grounded tactical companion intelligence, a modest support construct built for field units that runs on a cracked-glass lattice of salvaged relay cores. It guides its operators through hostile terrain by reading ambient signals and marking safe routes, and it is known for its unusually dry and loyal manner.

rites.name: Haledath
rites.text: Haledath is a set of armored harness-frames worn by the watch-wardens of Joroneldock's river delta, built from tempered brass and reactive gel. Each frame amplifies the wearer's muscle with pressure-stored springs, letting a warden hurl a loaded cart or leap a canal in a single bound.

rites.name: Pelordestar
rites.text: Pelordestar is a slender blade of humming alloy in the Joroneldock, forged by the Grounded smiths of the sixth era who tuned its core to a shivering flux. Its edge sings with a rapid, sustained vibration that loosens the bonds of whatever it touches, letting even stone part like wet clay.

rites.name: Zephisasha
rites.text: Zephisasha is a concept within the Joroneldock omniverse, arising in the Three Futures, where the ending forks and the Library shelves every outcome side by side. It is a thin, grounded idea about powers that hold their shape only while a single branch is being read.
